target_customer: Small and mid-sized inside sales teams, mostly startups and SMBs, that sell by phone and email
problem: Existing CRMs logged sales activity but did little to help reps make calls, send email and follow up at volume, so the founders built a CRM with calling and email at its core.

founders.name: Steli Efti
previous_startups: ElasticSales (outsourced sales firm, wound down after Close revenue passed services)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch April 2013 says Close.io grew out of ElasticSales, which had pivoted from SwipeGood. Education not found in opened sources.

founders.name: Anthony Nemitz
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder on the Close about page and YC page.

founders.name: Thomas Steinacher
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder on the Close about page; still hands-on in product development per that page.

technical_complexity.rationale: A web CRM with built-in calling and email sync was standard engineering with some hard parts (telephony and email integration) for a small team in 2013.

defensibility.rationale: CRMs create data switching costs, but many CRMs existed and the integrated dialer and email could be copied by others.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought Close. It stayed independent, reported as profitable and self funded on its own about page, and in 2019 bought the close.com domain.

market_need_then: The founders ran their own outsourced sales firm and found existing CRMs tracked sales but did not help them sell, then other startups asked to use the internal tool (Close about page, TechCrunch April 2013).

branding.name_origin: Not explained by the company. Close.io was chosen because close.com was held by another owner; the product was called Close internally and by customers.
branding.domain_note: Launched on close.io in 2013 because close.com was used by a social networking startup. Bought close.com in April 2019 after more than five years of follow ups; price not disclosed by Close (a wiki reports over $500K and a domain blog reports low six figures, unverified).

identity.voice_and_tone: Sales hustle voice from the CEO, with a large content and blog presence

branding.brand_signature: Steli Efti's sales-hustle content and the 2019 rebrand from Close.io to Close.com

rebrands.why: Company said it had outgrown the .io and wanted its public name to match what customers already called it

branding.community_and_virality: Founder led content and podcasts drove awareness; no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Solid founder-led brand in sales circles and a rare exact word .com, but a generic word and no evidence of broad cultural pull.

pivots.why: Internal CRM drew interest from other startups and software revenue passed services revenue

outcome_analysis: Close grew out of the founders' own outsourced sales firm, which gave them direct insight into what sales reps needed. After the 2013 launch it stayed small on outside capital, reports itself profitable and self funded, and kept about 120 to 130 remote staff. It has not been acquired and no layoffs were found. The main risk is a crowded CRM market dominated by Salesforce and HubSpot.
notes: Total raised conflicts across databases ($250K to $500K); Efti said in an interview they used convertible notes and some outside funding while the company calls itself self funded.
